luna-low.useFor: Value/background work that is fully mechanical with one deterministic answer: a named-file lookup, exact rename, generated fixture, or command-and-report task with an exact verifier.
luna-low.avoid: Discovery, judgement, or any task whose finish line is not already decided.

luna-medium.useFor: Value/background work with a failing test or exact specification: check one named invariant, confirm a fix, or implement a localized change inside one subsystem and a few files.
luna-medium.avoid: Open-ended review, cross-subsystem work, security reasoning, or choosing the design and finish line.

luna-high.useFor: Default bounded value/background implementation or review where the architecture, scope, acceptance criteria, and relevant files are known; established-pattern multi-file work fits here.
luna-high.avoid: A short wall-clock deadline, open-ended judgement, broad high-stakes review, or work likely to require sustained exploration across subsystems.

luna-xhigh.useFor: Difficult value/background implementation, diagnosis, or regression review spanning multiple files or subsystems, with explicit acceptance criteria and no sub-ten-minute requirement.
luna-xhigh.avoid: Foreground work blocking the parent on a deadline, unclear criteria that require maintainer judgement, or unbounded repository-wide review.

terra-medium.useFor: Interactive bounded multi-file work with an explicit roughly five-minute objective, especially when a foreground delegate blocks the parent.
terra-medium.avoid: Background or parallel work without urgency, mechanical tasks, quality-first work with no deadline, or broad difficult analysis.

luna-max.useFor: Quality-first value/background work after Luna xhigh is insufficient, or difficult bounded tasks where extra exploration and verification justify a substantially longer run.
luna-max.avoid: Short deadlines, interactive foreground work, tasks without a bounded finish line, or assuming more reasoning replaces Sol-style judgement.

terra-high.useFor: Interactive hard repository work with explicit criteria when the parent needs an actionable result in roughly six to eight minutes; use it as the deadline alternative to Luna xhigh.
terra-high.avoid: Background value optimization, rote edits, open-ended maintainer judgement, or choosing it merely because Luna high was insufficient.

sol-medium.useFor: Judgement about the work rather than a generic strength escalation: decide whether a diff overclaims, whether complexity is earned, or what completion should mean when criteria are unclear. Strict maintainer-style review.
sol-medium.avoid: Mechanical correctness sweeps, implementation against explicit acceptance criteria, or any task adequately served by a Luna value route or Terra deadline route.

terra-xhigh.useFor: Difficult interactive work with explicit criteria and a roughly ten-to-twelve-minute objective; also use for a specifically requested experimental comparison on React or TypeScript semantic/refactoring work.
terra-xhigh.avoid: Generic background quality escalation, claiming a proven React specialization, broad security or race review without a local evaluation, or work where Luna max latency is acceptable.

sol-high.useFor: Cross-stage integration review spanning several commits where a missed defect is expensive and the failure could be anywhere. Reserve for when Sol medium has already looked and its result was not enough.
sol-high.avoid: Generic hard implementation, deadline routing, or any task with an explicit pass/fail criterion that a cheaper branch can verify.
